name: Catoctin Mountain Park Loop (Chimney Rock, Wolf Rock, Hog Rock)
blurb: Full circuit from the visitor center linking Chimney Rock, Wolf Rock, Thurmont Vista, Blue Ridge Summit Overlook and Hog Rock, ending at Cunningham Falls. Signed but unblazed, so carry the park map.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Chimney Rock (Catoctin Mountain Park)
blurb: Stack of quartzite ledges with an open view south over the Catoctin ridges. A steady climb from the visitor center or the Park Central Road lot; usually paired with Wolf Rock.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Wolf Rock (Catoctin Mountain Park)
blurb: Long tilted slab of quartzite split by deep crevices that you scramble across. There is no wide view; the rock is the attraction. Half a mile along the ridge from Chimney Rock.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Hog Rock (Catoctin Mountain Park)
blurb: Rock ledge overlook a short walk from the Hog Rock lot on Park Central Road, on a loop trail through big hardwoods. An easy fall-color stop.

facts.dogs: leashed; not allowed on the rock formations

name: Thurmont Vista (Catoctin Mountain Park)
blurb: Cleared overlook facing east over Thurmont and the Monocacy Valley, reached by a short uphill trail from its own lot on Park Central Road.

name: Blue Ridge Summit Vista (Catoctin Mountain Park)
blurb: North-facing overlook toward Blue Ridge Summit and the Pennsylvania line, on the ridge trail between Hog Rock and Thurmont Vista. The quietest of the park vistas.

name: Cunningham Falls
blurb: Maryland's tallest cascading waterfall, 78 ft down a rock face on Big Hunting Creek. Walk in from the Hunting Creek Lake lot or take the boardwalk from the MD 77 roadside lot.

facts.fee: William Houck Area: $3-5 per person in season for MD residents (+$2 out of state); $3 per vehicle off-season

name: Hunting Creek Lake (Cunningham Falls State Park)
blurb: 43-acre mountain lake with sand swimming beaches, boat rentals and picnic lawns, in the William Houck Area. The trail to Cunningham Falls starts from the beach lot.

facts.fee: $3-5 per person in season for MD residents (+$2 out of state); $3 per vehicle off-season

name: Cat Rock (Cunningham Falls State Park)
blurb: Steep climb from MD 77 to a pile of quartzite blocks; scramble on top for a view in every direction. Far fewer people than the national park side of the road.

name: Bob's Hill Overlooks (Cunningham Falls State Park)
blurb: Climb the Catoctin Trail from the Manor Area to two short spur trails, one ledge facing north and one facing south over the Frederick Valley.

facts.fee: Manor Area: $3 per vehicle MD residents, $5 out of state

name: Catoctin Furnace
blurb: Stone stack of an iron furnace that shut down in 1903, with the ruined ironmaster's house and a footbridge trail over US 15 into the state park's Manor Area.

name: Gambrill State Park (High Knob overlooks)
blurb: Stone overlooks built by the CCC in the 1930s on High Knob: one looks east over Frederick, another west across the Middletown Valley to South Mountain. Trail loops start nearby.

facts.fee: $3 per vehicle MD residents, $5 out of state

name: Sugarloaf Mountain
blurb: Lone 1,283-ft mountain standing about 800 ft above the farmland. A road climbs to overlook lots and short rocky trails reach the summit. Privately owned land kept open to the public.

name: Monocacy National Battlefield
blurb: 1864 battlefield straddling the Monocacy River with farm-lane walking loops at the Worthington, Thomas and Best farms. Quiet river and field scenery just off I-270.

name: Loys Station Covered Bridge
blurb: Covered bridge over Owens Creek, rebuilt with its surviving timbers after a 1991 arson fire, set in a small park with picnic tables and creek access.

name: Roddy Road Covered Bridge
blurb: One-lane king post covered bridge only 40 ft long, built in the 1850s over Owens Creek, with a small creekside park next to it.

name: Utica Mills Covered Bridge
blurb: Burr truss covered bridge first built in 1834 over the Monocacy; the half that survived an 1889 flood was moved here to Fishing Creek. Still open to cars.

name: Monocacy Aqueduct (C&O Canal)
blurb: The largest aqueduct on the C&O Canal: 438 ft of stone arches carrying the towpath over the Monocacy River where it meets the Potomac. Walk across; boat ramp beside it.

name: National Shrine Grotto of Our Lady of Lourdes
blurb: Mountainside shrine above Mount St. Mary's with a replica of the Lourdes grotto, shaded garden paths, a pool and a valley view from the terrace.

name: Baker Park and Carroll Creek Park
blurb: Downtown Frederick's main park with a carillon tower and Culler Lake, linked to the Carroll Creek promenade of brick walks, footbridges and water-lily plantings.

name: Fountain Rock Park
blurb: Row of old stone lime kilns beside a spring-fed quarry pond, with a small nature center. A short, flat walk.

name: Gathland State Park
blurb: Ruins of a Civil War correspondent's mountaintop estate and his stone War Correspondents Memorial Arch, right on the Appalachian Trail at Crampton's Gap.

facts.fee: free

name: Maryland Heights (Harpers Ferry)
blurb: Steep climb to a cliff straight above Harpers Ferry and the two rivers; the longer loop adds the Civil War stone fort. Fall 2026: Lower Town footbridge closed for repairs, NPS shuttle runs to Lock 34.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Weverton Cliffs
blurb: Switchbacks on the Appalachian Trail from the Weverton Road lot lead to open cliffs high above the Potomac, looking upriver toward Harpers Ferry. Short and steep.

name: Annapolis Rock (Appalachian Trail)
blurb: Appalachian Trail north from the US 40 lot to a west-facing cliff over Greenbrier Lake and the Cumberland Valley. Continue to Black Rock Cliff for the full 7.1-mile out-and-back.

facts.fee: free

name: Black Rock Cliff (Appalachian Trail)
blurb: Wide west-facing cliff with a talus field below, about a mile past Annapolis Rock on the AT and usually much quieter.

name: Washington Monument State Park
blurb: The first monument to George Washington, a 40-ft stone tower built by Boonsboro townspeople in 1827 on South Mountain. Climb the inside stairs for a valley view; the AT passes the base.

facts.fee: $2 per vehicle MD residents, $4 out of state

name: Greenbrier State Park
blurb: 42-acre lake under South Mountain with a long sand swimming beach, boat rentals and trails that link to the AT. Summer weekends need a day-use reservation.

facts.fee: $3-5 per person in summer for MD residents (+$2 out of state); $3 per vehicle off-season; reservation required weekends and holidays Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: Antietam National Battlefield
blurb: Preserved 1862 battlefield of farm lanes, rail fences and stone bridges along Antietam Creek. Walk the Cornfield and Bloody Lane trails or follow the tour road.

name: Burnside Bridge (Antietam)
blurb: Stone arch bridge of 1836 over Antietam Creek, fought over for hours in 1862. An overlook sits above it and creekside trails loop out from the bridge.

name: Bloody Lane Observation Tower (Antietam)
blurb: Stone War Department tower at the end of the Sunken Road. Climb it for a full view of the battlefield with South Mountain on the horizon.

name: Fort Frederick State Park
blurb: Massive stone fort from the French and Indian War with restored walls and barracks, beside the Potomac, the C&O Canal and Big Pool.

facts.fee: $3 per vehicle MD residents, $5 out of state

name: Crystal Grottoes Caverns
blurb: Maryland's only show cave: guided walks through narrow passages crowded with formations. Privately run with paid admission; check hours before driving out.

facts.fee: paid guided tour

name: Devil's Backbone County Park
blurb: Small county park where Antietam Creek bends around a narrow rock ridge: a dam, a footbridge, canoe access, fishing and picnic tables under big sycamores.

name: High Rock (Pen Mar)
blurb: Graffiti-covered cliff on South Mountain, a former resort observatory site and now a hang-glider launch, with a wide view west over the Cumberland Valley. Parking is right beside it.

name: Pen Mar Park
blurb: County park beside the Mason-Dixon Line on the site of an old mountain resort: overlook pavilion facing west, picnic grounds and the Appalachian Trail. Open May through October, 9 am to sunset.

name: Big Slackwater (C&O Canal at McMahon's Mill)
blurb: Where canal boats once left the canal for the river, the towpath now runs on a concrete walkway under limestone cliffs at the Potomac's edge. Start at the old mill and walk downstream.

name: Dam 4 (C&O Canal)
blurb: Stone canal dam with the whole Potomac pouring over it, a winch house and an old hydro plant on the far bank. Flatwater paddling above, fishing below.

name: Dam 5 (C&O Canal)
blurb: Canal feeder dam across the Potomac with a lockhouse and inlet lock at the end of a quiet road. Loud water and little company.

name: Four Locks (C&O Canal)
blurb: Four lift locks in a row where the canal cut across a river bend, with a lockhouse, mule barn and boat ramp left from the canal community that stood here.

name: Cushwa Basin and Conococheague Aqueduct
blurb: Canal hub at Williamsport: a re-watered stone aqueduct, turning basin, lift lock and warehouse visitor center within a short walk on the towpath.

name: Killiansburg Cave (C&O Canal)
blurb: Shallow cave in the bluff above the towpath where Sharpsburg civilians sheltered during the Battle of Antietam. Reached by walking the towpath from Snyders Landing.

name: Antietam Creek Aqueduct (C&O Canal)
blurb: Three-arch stone aqueduct carrying the towpath over the mouth of Antietam Creek, next to a walk-in riverside campground.

name: Western Maryland Rail Trail
blurb: 28 miles of paved rail trail between Fort Frederick and Little Orleans, shadowing the C&O Canal and the Potomac through Hancock.

name: Sideling Hill Road Cut
blurb: I-68 passes through a 340-ft-deep notch blasted out of Sideling Hill, exposing rock layers bent into a giant U. Pull into the rest area and walk up to the viewing platforms.

facts.fee: free

name: Round Top Cement Mill ruins
blurb: Brick chimney, kilns and mine openings of a 19th-century cement works squeezed between the rail trail and the canal, a few miles west of Hancock.

name: Wilson Bridge
blurb: Five-arch limestone bridge of 1819 over Conococheague Creek, 210 ft long and the longest of the county's old stone bridges. It carried the National Road.

name: Hagerstown City Park
blurb: City park around a spring-fed lake with swans, a walking loop, an art museum and a steam locomotive on display.

name: Paw Paw Tunnel (C&O Canal)
blurb: 3,118-ft brick-lined canal tunnel you walk through by flashlight on the old towpath, with a rock gorge at the far end. Return over the top on the steep 2-mile Tunnel Hill Trail.

name: Point Lookout Overlook (Green Ridge State Forest)
blurb: View at about 900 ft over a horseshoe bend of the Potomac and the West Virginia ridges, used as a Union lookout in the Civil War. On unpaved Carroll Road, off Oldtown Road.
coord_source: none found (not in OpenStreetMap, GNIS or Nominatim); take it from the forest's overlook driving map

name: Banner's Overlook (Green Ridge State Forest)
blurb: Overlook at 1,650 ft on Mertens Avenue near the center of the forest, looking east toward the Potomac and the West Virginia ridges. Named for an early forest warden.

name: Green Ridge State Forest Headquarters Overlook
blurb: Wooden platform behind the forest headquarters just off I-68 with a first look across the ridges. Pick up the overlook driving map and campsite permits here.

name: Rocky Gap State Park (Lake Habeeb)
blurb: 243-acre Lake Habeeb at the foot of Evitts Mountain with three public sand beaches, boat rentals and a trail around the shore. Summer weekends need a day-use reservation.

facts.fee: $2 per vehicle to $4 per person depending on season; reservation required weekends and holidays Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: Rocky Gap Gorge (Canyon Overlook Trail)
blurb: Short trail near the dam to a ledge over the gorge that Rocky Gap Run cut through the mountain, lined with hemlock and rhododendron.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap, Rocky Gap Dam next to the trail)

name: Dan's Rock Overlook
blurb: Painted rock outcrop at 2,895 ft, the highest point in Allegany County, with a long view east over the Potomac valley. A paved road goes to the top.

name: The Narrows and Lovers Leap
blurb: Water gap where Wills Creek, the National Road and the railroads squeeze between quartzite cliffs. Lovers Leap on the rim is reached by an unmarked path and closes for falcon nesting.

name: Canal Place (C&O Canal terminus)
blurb: Western end of the 184.5-mile C&O Canal towpath and starting point of the Great Allegheny Passage, beside the scenic railroad station in downtown Cumberland.

name: Great Allegheny Passage: Brush Tunnel
blurb: The rail trail climbs out of Cumberland through the Narrows, past the Cumberland Bone Cave, then through the 914-ft Brush Tunnel, which it shares with a steam tourist train.

name: Mason-Dixon Line marker (Great Allegheny Passage)
blurb: The Maryland-Pennsylvania border marked across the rail trail with stone blocks, between Frostburg and Big Savage Tunnel, with a long view down the valley.

name: Oldtown Low-Water Toll Bridge
blurb: Privately owned one-lane bridge sitting just above the Potomac, where a toll is collected for crossing to West Virginia. The C&O Canal towpath crosses its approach.

name: Lonaconing Iron Furnace
blurb: Sandstone furnace stack 50 ft high that first made iron in 1839, standing in a small park in the middle of town.

name: LaVale Toll Gate House
blurb: Seven-sided brick toll house built in 1835-36 on the National Road. A quick roadside stop.

name: Dans Mountain State Park
blurb: 482-acre park high on Dans Mountain above the Georges Creek valley, with a summer swimming pool, picnic areas and a fishing pond.

facts.fee: free

name: Muddy Creek Falls
blurb: Maryland's tallest free-falling waterfall, a 54-ft drop reached by a short walk through old hemlocks, with decks at top and bottom. Summer weekends need a day-use reservation.

facts.fee: $3 per person MD residents, $5 out of state in season and on May, Sept and Oct weekends; $3 per car other times; reservation required weekends and holidays Memorial Day-Labor Day

name: Swallow Falls (Canyon Trail)
blurb: The Youghiogheny drops over broad sandstone ledges; people wade and swim in the pools below in summer. Part of the canyon loop through hemlocks more than 300 years old.

facts.fee: same day-use charge as Muddy Creek Falls

name: Tolliver Falls
blurb: Small ledge fall on Tolliver Run in a shaded hemlock hollow, the quietest stop on the Swallow Falls canyon loop.

name: Herrington Manor State Park
blurb: 53-acre Herrington Lake with a sand beach, boat rentals and log cabins, ringed by pine forest a few miles from Swallow Falls.

facts.fee: $3 per person MD residents, $5 out of state in summer and on weekends; $3 per vehicle off-season

name: Deep Creek Lake State Park
blurb: Public beach, boat launch and discovery center on the northeast shore of Maryland's big mountain reservoir, with trails climbing Meadow Mountain behind.

facts.fee: $3-5 per person in season; $3 per vehicle MD residents off-season

name: New Germany State Park
blurb: Small lake in a hemlock valley with a swimming area, cabins and a web of easy forest trails that turn into ski trails in winter.

facts.fee: free

name: Big Run State Park and Savage River Reservoir
blurb: Primitive campsites where Big Run and Monroe Run meet at the head of the 360-acre Savage River Reservoir, deep in state forest. Quiet paddling and trout fishing.

facts.fee: free day use

name: Monroe Run Overlook
blurb: Roadside overlook near the crest of Meadow Mountain on New Germany Road, looking down the forested Monroe Run valley. Best in October.

name: Cranesville Swamp Preserve
blurb: Boreal bog in a frost pocket on the Maryland-West Virginia line, with plants normally found far to the north. Five short trails and a 1,500-ft boardwalk over the wettest part.

facts.fee: free

name: Hoye-Crest (Maryland high point)
blurb: Maryland's highest point, 3,360 ft on Backbone Mountain, reached only from West Virginia: a steep mile up an old road from roadside parking on US 219 to a cairn, mailbox and view east.

name: Kendall Trail (Youghiogheny River)
blurb: 1890s railroad grade heading upstream along the wild Youghiogheny to the site of the logging town of Kendall, with many places to reach the river and swim. Water rises fast on dam-release days.

name: Casselman River Bridge State Park
blurb: Stone bridge built in 1813-14 for the National Road; its 80-ft span was the largest stone arch in America at the time. Walk over it, then visit the artisan village next door.

name: Finzel Swamp Preserve
blurb: Nature Conservancy wetland at the head of the Savage River with tamarack and other northern holdovers. A trail crosses the swamp on short wooden bridges to a shallow pond.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap wetland 'Cranberry Swamp', via Photon geocoder)

name: Lostland Run Trail (Potomac State Forest)
blurb: Trail following Lostland Run down to the North Branch Potomac, passing Cascade Falls, a swinging bridge and a rock overlook of the river. Reached on gravel forest roads.

name: Rock Maze (Garrett State Forest)
blurb: Field of house-sized sandstone blocks split by passages wide and narrow that you can wander through. Short path from Snaggy Mountain Road, near Swallow Falls.

name: Broadford Lake Park
blurb: Town-run lake park just outside Oakland with a beach and swimming area and cheap canoe, kayak and paddle-boat rentals. Open Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day weekend.

facts.fee: $4 per car weekdays, $5 weekends

name: Sang Run State Park
blurb: 264-acre park at a put-in for the Upper Yough's Class V whitewater, with an early-1800s homestead, the old Friends Store and river meadow trails.

name: Harpers Ferry Lower Town and The Point
blurb: Restored 19th-century streets of John Brown's raid ending at The Point, where the Shenandoah meets the Potomac under the cliffs of Maryland and Loudoun Heights. Park at the visitor center and ride the shuttle.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Jefferson Rock
blurb: Shale slabs on the Appalachian Trail above Lower Town looking down the Shenandoah to the water gap, the view Thomas Jefferson praised. Short climb up stone steps past church ruins.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

name: Loudoun Heights and Split Rock
blurb: Cross the Shenandoah on the AT and climb the Blue Ridge to Split Rock, a ledge looking straight at Harpers Ferry and Maryland Heights. Quieter than its neighbor across the river.

facts.fee: $20 per vehicle or $10 per person, valid 3 days

coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap, Split Rock viewpoint; hike starts in Lower Town)

name: Bolivar Heights
blurb: Open ridge with Civil War earthworks and cannon and a clear view east through the Harpers Ferry water gap. Easy mowed loops from the lot.

name: Murphy-Chambers Farm
blurb: Farm-field loop to a bluff overlook above the Shenandoah River, past Civil War earthworks and the site where John Brown's fort once stood.

name: Virginius Island ruins
blurb: Flat walk from Lower Town among the stone foundations, mill races and walls of a 19th-century factory village on a 12-acre island in the Shenandoah.

name: Shannondale Springs Wildlife Management Area
blurb: Site of a mineral springs resort founded in 1820 on a bend of the Shenandoah River upstream of Harpers Ferry, now public hunting and fishing land with river access.

name: Cacapon Resort State Park
blurb: 6,115-acre park on the east slope of Cacapon Mountain with a small lake and beach, lodge and miles of ridge trails.

name: Cacapon Mountain Overlook
blurb: Overlook at 2,320 ft on the crest of Cacapon Mountain, the highest point in the park and in Morgan County, reached by the park's mountain road or by trail.

name: Berkeley Springs State Park
blurb: Warm mineral springs in a small town-center park that George Washington first visited in 1748. Wade in the stone-lined channels for free or book a soak in the 1815 Roman Bathhouse.

name: Prospect Peak (Panorama Overlook)
blurb: Roadside pull-off on WV 9 west of Berkeley Springs looking down on the Potomac and Cacapon rivers with Maryland and Pennsylvania ridges behind. No walking needed.

name: Ice Mountain Preserve
blurb: Talus slope whose vents breathe cold air all summer, keeping ice into the warm months and sheltering northern plants. Visits are guided only: book a Nature Conservancy docent hike weeks ahead.

name: Sleepy Creek Lake
blurb: 205-acre lake inside the 22,928-acre Sleepy Creek Wildlife Management Area, with primitive lakeside campsites and long gravel approach roads.

name: Yankauer Nature Preserve
blurb: Audubon preserve with easy loop trails through cedar and hardwood forest to a bluff above the Potomac. Good spring wildflowers.

name: Rumsey Monument Park
blurb: Tall column on a bluff above the Potomac marking where James Rumsey demonstrated his steamboat in 1787. Short walk from Shepherdstown's main street.

name: Cranny Crow Overlook (Lost River State Park)
blurb: Rock ledge at 3,200 ft on Big Ridge with a view over five counties. The climb starts at the White Oak trailhead by the stables; a longer loop adds Cheeks Rock and the old fire tower.

name: Trout Pond Recreation Area (Rockcliff Lake)
blurb: Forest Service lake with a sand swimming beach, next to tiny Trout Pond, West Virginia's only natural lake. Campground and trails up Long Mountain.

name: Big Schloss
blurb: Climb from Wolf Gap along the state-line ridge to a white sandstone outcrop at 2,964 ft, reached by a wooden footbridge, with views over Trout Run Valley and the Shenandoah Valley.

facts.fee: free

name: Tibbet Knob
blurb: The other hike from Wolf Gap: shorter, with two steep rock scrambles near the top and a wide ledge looking north and west over Trout Run Valley. Fewer people than Big Schloss.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap summit; trailhead is Wolf Gap, 38.9235, -78.6895)

name: Halfmoon Lookout
blurb: Loop up Halfmoon Mountain to a rocky point with the stone base of an old fire lookout and a sweeping view down Trout Run Valley.

name: The Trough (South Branch Potomac)
blurb: Six-mile roadless gorge of the South Branch between Romney and Moorefield, known for bald eagles. Seen only by canoe or kayak, or from the excursion train that runs through it.

name: Hanging Rocks
blurb: Vertical cliffs rising nearly 300 ft from the South Branch Potomac where WV 28 and the railroad squeeze past, four miles north of Romney.

name: Fort Mill Ridge Civil War Trenches
blurb: Well-preserved Civil War trenches on a wooded ridge above the South Branch, dug to guard the approaches to Romney. Short interpretive loop.

name: Nancy Hanks Memorial
blurb: Small memorial far up a narrow hollow road on Mikes Run, at the traditional birthplace of Nancy Hanks, mother of Abraham Lincoln.

name: Jennings Randolph Lake: Waffle Rock and West Virginia Overlook
blurb: Boulder with a raised waffle-grid pattern weathered into the sandstone, displayed at the Corps of Engineers overlook above the 952-acre lake on the North Branch Potomac.

name: Greenland Gap Preserve
blurb: Deep gap through New Creek Mountain ringed by sandstone cliffs about 800 ft above the creek. A Nature Conservancy preserve with no maintained trails; two rough paths climb to the cliff tops.

facts.fee: free

name: Smoke Hole Canyon (Big Bend)
blurb: Narrow road following the South Branch Potomac through a 20-mile gorge walled by Cave Mountain and North Fork Mountain, ending at Big Bend Campground inside a loop of the river.

name: Eagle Rock (Smoke Hole)
blurb: Tall fin of rock rising straight from the South Branch beside Smoke Hole Road, with a deep pool at its base. An easy pull-off inside the canyon.

name: Chimney Top (North Fork Mountain)
blurb: Relentless climb from Smoke Hole Road up the north end of North Fork Mountain to sandstone towers and a cliff-edge view down the North Fork valley to the Allegheny Front.

name: Seneca Rocks
blurb: Blade of white quartzite standing 900 ft over the North Fork. A graded trail with switchbacks and steps climbs to a platform near the top; the exposed summit ridge beyond is a scramble.

name: Champe Rocks
blurb: Twin quartzite crags like a smaller Seneca Rocks, standing over the North Fork a few miles north on WV 28. Viewed from the road.

name: Seneca Caverns
blurb: Show cave in Germany Valley with guided tours going 165 ft underground. Seasonal: in 2026 it opened May 1 on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays only.

facts.fee: paid guided tour

name: Smoke Hole Caverns
blurb: Commercial show cave on WV 28 west of Petersburg, open since 1940, with guided tours past dense formations.

facts.fee: paid guided tour

name: Spruce Knob
blurb: West Virginia's highest point at 4,863 ft: drive to the top, then walk the half-mile loop through wind-bent red spruce and boulder fields to a stone lookout tower.

name: Spruce Knob Lake
blurb: Small trout lake high on the west side of Spruce Mountain, with a walk-around trail and a campground nearby. Very dark night skies.

name: Upper Falls of Seneca Creek
blurb: Seneca Creek Trail drops gently through spruce and old meadows, with stream crossings, to the Upper Falls and a run of cascades. A long day hike or a classic overnight.

name: Germany Valley Overlook
blurb: Pull-off on US 33 climbing North Fork Mountain, looking across the farms and limestone ridges of Germany Valley toward Spruce Mountain.

name: Bear Rocks Preserve (Dolly Sods)
blurb: Wind-carved sandstone outcrops and heath barrens on the rim of the Allegheny Front, looking east over ridge after ridge. Steps from the parking area; Forest Road 75 is gated from about January to April.

name: Bear Rocks Trail (Dolly Sods North)
blurb: Out across the open plateau of Dolly Sods North: blueberry heath, bogs, a ford of Red Creek and wide meadows on the way to Raven Ridge. Expect mud and wind.

name: Lions Head (Dolly Sods Wilderness)
blurb: Sandstone prow on Breathed Mountain overlooking the Red Creek canyon. Usually climbed from the Red Creek trailhead at Laneville; the last pitch is an unmarked path among boulders.

name: Rohrbaugh Cliffs (Dolly Sods Wilderness)
blurb: Mostly level walk through spruce, rhododendron and rocky meadows to open cliffs above the Red Creek basin, facing Lions Head across the canyon.

name: Forks of Red Creek (Dolly Sods Wilderness)
blurb: Loop from the Blackbird Knob trailhead down to where the forks of Red Creek meet in a run of small waterfalls and swimming holes, with campsites beside the water.

name: Red Creek Trail (Laneville trailhead)
blurb: Low-elevation way into Dolly Sods that stays reachable when the forest roads are gated for winter. The trail follows Red Creek upstream past pools and fords toward the Forks and Lions Head.

name: Table Rock (Canaan Mountain)
blurb: Flat sandstone ledge on the rim of Canaan Mountain with a huge view over the Dry Fork valley. A short, rooty trail from Canaan Loop Road, which is rough gravel.

name: Canaan Valley Resort State Park
blurb: State park in a high, bathtub-shaped valley of wetlands and spruce: easy meadow and boardwalk trails, deer everywhere, and a chairlift ride up to Bald Knob for the view.

name: Freeland Boardwalk (Canaan Valley National Wildlife Refuge)
blurb: Half-mile boardwalk loop over beaver ponds and wet meadows on the valley floor. Good for birds and for a flat walk after a hard hike.

name: Blackwater Falls
blurb: The tea-colored Blackwater River drops 57 ft into its canyon. A long staircase and boardwalk lead to decks at the base; an easier paved path reaches an overlook on the far side.

name: Lindy Point
blurb: Railed platform on a rock tower jutting into Blackwater Canyon, reached by a short flat path through rhododendron. The standard sunset spot in the park.

name: Elakala Falls
blurb: First of four falls on Shays Run as it tumbles into Blackwater Canyon, a few minutes from the lodge with a footbridge across its lip. The lower falls need a steep scramble.

name: Pendleton Point Overlook
blurb: Drive-up overlook at the deepest, widest part of Blackwater Canyon, looking across to the lodge and down to the river.

name: Pase Point
blurb: Rock point above the junction of the Blackwater and North Fork canyons, reached by a quiet forest trail from the north-rim side of the park.

name: Douglas Falls
blurb: Broad fall on the North Fork of the Blackwater pouring over ledges stained orange by old mine drainage, below Thomas on the Blackwater Canyon rail trail, past rows of coke ovens.

name: Olson Observation Tower
blurb: Steel fire tower on Backbone Mountain that you can climb for a full-circle view over the Blackwater Canyon rim and the Cheat River country. Reached by a gravel forest road off US 219.

name: Otter Creek Wilderness
blurb: Roadless bowl between McGowan and Shavers mountains with 45 miles of unblazed trails. The 11-mile Otter Creek Trail follows the stream past cascades and deep pools, with several fords.
coord_source: wikipedia (centre of the wilderness, not a trailhead)

name: Fairfax Stone State Park
blurb: Boundary stone at the spring where the North Branch of the Potomac begins, first set in 1746 to settle the limits of Lord Fairfax's land grant.

name: Cathedral State Park
blurb: 132 acres of old-growth hemlock right beside US 50, the largest stand of virgin timber left in West Virginia. Flat loop trails along Rhine Creek.

name: Coopers Rock Overlook
blurb: Sandstone promontory with a footbridge and railings high above the Cheat River canyon, with boulder mazes just behind it. The entrance road is closed December 31 to March 31; walk in from the I-68 lot.

name: Raven Rock (Coopers Rock State Forest)
blurb: Forest-road walk to a second clifftop over the Cheat gorge, with the same river view as the main overlook and a fraction of the visitors.

name: Henry Clay Iron Furnace
blurb: Stone furnace 30 ft square and 30 ft high, built in 1834-36, standing alone in the woods of Coopers Rock State Forest at the end of a downhill trail.

name: Pole Steeple
blurb: Short, steep trail from Railroad Bed Road to a quartzite cliff nearly 500 ft above Laurel Lake, with the whole Pine Grove Furnace valley below.

name: Sunset Rocks
blurb: Loop from Pine Grove Furnace on the Appalachian Trail and a boulder-scramble spur along Little Rocky Ridge to a south-facing ledge, passing the AT halfway marker and the turn for Camp Michaux.
coord_source: other (OpenStreetMap, Sunset Rocks outcrop; loop starts at the Pine Grove Furnace AT lot)

name: Hammonds Rocks
blurb: Cluster of quartzite outcrops on the crest of South Mountain right beside Ridge Road. Scramble up for views north over the Cumberland Valley.

name: Chimney Rocks (Michaux State Forest)
blurb: Appalachian Trail climb from Old Forge to a jagged outcrop on Buzzard Peak, looking out over the Waynesboro Reservoir and the folds of South Mountain.

name: Long Pine Run Reservoir
blurb: Quiet reservoir ringed by pine and oak in Michaux State Forest, with a boat launch. Popular for paddling, fishing and walks along the shore.

name: Caledonia State Park
blurb: 1,125-acre park on US 30 around the site of Thaddeus Stevens's iron furnace: reconstructed stack, creekside trails, a swimming pool and the Appalachian Trail passing through.

name: Fuller Lake (Pine Grove Furnace State Park)
blurb: Small, cold, clear lake filling the old iron-ore pit of Pine Grove Furnace, with a sand beach a short walk from the furnace stack, the general store and the AT.

name: Laurel Lake (Pine Grove Furnace State Park)
blurb: The larger of the park's two lakes, with a sand beach, boat rentals and Pole Steeple's cliff visible above the far shore.

name: Appalachian Trail Museum and halfway point
blurb: Old stone mill turned museum of the Appalachian Trail, at the trail's traditional halfway stop, where thru-hikers attempt to eat a half gallon of ice cream at the general store.

name: Kings Gap Environmental Education Center
blurb: Stone mansion on top of South Mountain with a terrace view over the Cumberland Valley, a walled garden, and quiet trails across 2,531 acres of oak and pine.

name: Mont Alto State Park
blurb: Pennsylvania's oldest state park: a 24-acre picnic grove on PA 233 with a distinctive old pavilion and a trout stream, surrounded by Michaux State Forest.

name: White Rocks (South Mountain)
blurb: Steep trail to a spine of white quartzite at the northern tip of South Mountain, with views over the Cumberland Valley; the spur joins the Appalachian Trail on the ridge.

name: Children's Lake (Boiling Springs)
blurb: Spring-fed village lake with a level path around it, an old iron furnace stack, and the Appalachian Trail running along the shore.

name: Camp Michaux ruins
blurb: Foundations, a stone barn wall and other remains of a secret World War II camp where German prisoners were interrogated, later a church camp. Self-guided walk in the state forest.

name: Devil's Den (Gettysburg)
blurb: Hill of house-sized boulders with passages and crevices to climb through, used by sharpshooters on the second day of the battle. Faces Little Round Top across the valley.

name: Little Round Top (Gettysburg)
blurb: Rocky hill at the Union left flank with paths among boulders and monuments and the widest view over the battlefield, west toward South Mountain.

name: Big Round Top (Gettysburg)
blurb: Wooded, boulder-strewn hill that is the highest point on the battlefield. A short steep path climbs to the summit; quiet compared with its neighbor.

name: Sachs Covered Bridge
blurb: 100-ft lattice-truss covered bridge over Marsh Creek, crossed by troops of both armies in 1863. Open to walkers only.

name: Culp's Hill Observation Tower (Gettysburg)
blurb: Steel War Department tower on the wooded hill that anchored the Union right. Climb it for a view over the town and the fields to the east.

name: Strawberry Hill Nature Preserve
blurb: Nonprofit preserve in the hills west of Gettysburg with streamside trails, ponds and rocky mountain forest, bordering Michaux State Forest.

name: Codorus State Park
blurb: 3,500-acre park around 1,275-acre Lake Marburg, with boat rentals, sailing, long shoreline trails and a large swimming pool in summer.

name: Gifford Pinchot State Park
blurb: 2,338-acre park around Pinchot Lake with a lake swimming beach, boat rentals and trails through fields of rounded diabase boulders.

name: Rocky Ridge County Park
blurb: Wooded ridge park north of York with observation decks facing north and south, a fall hawk watch and miles of trail.

name: Samuel S. Lewis State Park
blurb: 85-acre hilltop park on 885-ft Mt. Pisgah. Open lawns look out over the Susquehanna River valley; popular for kites, picnics and sunsets.

name: Highpoint Scenic Vista
blurb: Bald grass hilltop with a paved path spiraling to the summit and a full-circle view of the Susquehanna and the Wrightsville bridges.

name: Native Lands County Park
blurb: Trail across the hillside site of the last Susquehannock town, with river views, running along the Mason-Dixon Trail between Klines Run Park and Long Level.

name: Otter Creek and Urey Overlook
blurb: Mason-Dixon Trail through a rocky hemlock glen along Otter Creek, then a climb to Urey Overlook above the Susquehanna. Rough, strenuous footing and limited parking.

name: Mill Creek Falls Nature Preserve
blurb: Red-blazed trail dropping 240 ft from the lot to a 10-ft waterfall where two creeks meet just above the Susquehanna. Also has a mile-long accessible crushed-stone loop.

name: Lock 12 Historic Area
blurb: Intact stone lock of the Susquehanna and Tidewater Canal with lime kilns and sawmill ruins, in a shady picnic grove below Holtwood Dam.

name: Apollo County Park
blurb: Undeveloped county park of steep wooded ravines dropping to the Susquehanna, crossed by the Mason-Dixon Trail. Rugged and little used.

name: Indian Steps Museum
blurb: Riverside cabin from the early 1900s with thousands of Native American artifacts set into its walls, on wooded grounds beside the Susquehanna. Limited seasonal hours.

name: William H. Kain County Park (Lake Redman)
blurb: Two water-supply lakes just south of York with boat rentals, a bird-viewing area and miles of shoreline trail.

name: Howard Tunnel (Heritage Rail Trail)
blurb: 275-ft brick-lined railroad tunnel in use since 1838, the second-oldest active rail tunnel in the country. The rail trail runs through it beside the track.

name: Susquehanna Riverlands State Park (Schull's Rock)
blurb: Wooded 1,044-acre state park created in 2022 where Codorus Creek meets the Susquehanna. The Mason-Dixon Trail runs 2.75 miles through it past a rock overlook. No restrooms; park off River Farm Road.

name: Codorus Furnace
blurb: Stone iron furnace from about 1836 standing beside the road near the mouth of Codorus Creek. A two-minute stop.

name: Pinnacle Overlook
blurb: Rocky bluff 380 ft above Lake Aldred on the Susquehanna, with picnic tables at the rim and trail links to Kelly's Run and Tucquan Glen. Now part of Susquehannock State Park.

name: Tucquan Glen Nature Preserve
blurb: Ravine of rhododendron and hemlock where Tucquan Creek tumbles to the Susquehanna. The Conservancy lists the River Road lots as closed: hike in from Pinnacle Overlook, 4 miles round trip.

name: Kelly's Run Nature Preserve
blurb: Steep loop into a boulder-filled ravine with several stream crossings, on a national recreation trail that doubles as the Conestoga Trail.

name: Susquehannock State Park (Hawk Point)
blurb: Overlooks on a wooded plateau high above the Susquehanna and Conowingo Reservoir. Hawk Point looks down on river islands where bald eagles nest; Wissler Run Overlook is a short walk away.

name: Holtwood Dam and Face Rock Overlook
blurb: Overlook down onto Holtwood Dam, built 1905-10 and the oldest of the three big dams on the lower Susquehanna, and the scoured bedrock below it.

name: Shenks Ferry Wildflower Preserve
blurb: Sheltered ravine along Grubb Run with more than 70 species of wildflowers; best from late March into May. An easy path follows the stream.

name: House Rock and Wind Cave (Clark Nature Preserve)
blurb: Conestoga Trail climb from Pequea to House Rock's view over the Susquehanna, passing Wind Cave, a fracture cave in the hillside. The return trip involves a lot of up and down.

name: Climbers Run Nature Center
blurb: Lancaster Conservancy preserve and nature center on a restored trout stream, with easy loops through woods and meadow.

name: Ferncliff Wildlife and Wildflower Preserve
blurb: Old woods road following Barnes Run down a steep ravine to the Susquehanna. A Lancaster Conservancy preserve known for spring wildflowers and ferns.

name: Muddy Run Recreation Park
blurb: Power-company park around a recreation lake beside the pumped-storage reservoir, with a campground, boat rentals and trails.

name: Chickies Rock
blurb: Quartzite cliff above the Susquehanna north of Columbia, described as the largest exposed anticline on the East Coast. A short overlook trail leads from the PA 441 lot; Breezyview Overlook is nearby.

name: Columbia Crossing River Trails Center
blurb: Riverfront trailhead under the mile-long concrete-arch Veterans Memorial Bridge, start of the Northwest Lancaster County River Trail.

name: White Cliffs of Conoy
blurb: Chalk-white bluffs of limestone quarry waste dumped beside the Susquehanna. Walk or bike 1.5 flat, paved miles south from Koser Park on the river trail.

name: Safe Harbor Trestle (Enola Low Grade Trail)
blurb: Former railroad trestle high over the mouth of the Conestoga River, now decked for walkers and cyclists, with Safe Harbor Dam and the Susquehanna in view.

name: Martic Forge Trestle (Enola Low Grade Trail)
blurb: Long rail-trail bridge crossing high above Pequea Creek and the road at Martic Forge.

name: Turkey Hill Trail and overlooks
blurb: Strenuous ridge trail with river overlooks at both ends; the northern one looks over the Conejohela Flats, a waterfowl stopover. Loop back on the level Enola Low Grade rail trail.

name: Lancaster County Central Park
blurb: Large county park on the Conestoga River at the edge of Lancaster, with wooded trails, a garden of five senses and a covered bridge.

name: Nottingham County Park serpentine barrens
blurb: Pitch pine and prairie grass growing on green serpentine bedrock that poisons ordinary forest, a landscape unlike the farmland around it, dotted with old chrome and feldspar pits.

name: Wolf's Hollow County Park
blurb: Wooded hollow along Octoraro Creek with several miles of trail, a small waterfall and old mill ruins. Just east of the Lancaster County line.

name: Governor Dick Observation Tower
blurb: Concrete tower on a wooded hilltop; climb the ladders inside to a caged platform above the trees with views over several counties. Reached by forest trails from the nature center.

name: Middle Creek Wildlife Management Area
blurb: 6,000 acres of lakes and fields managed by the Game Commission. In late winter the main lake can hold up to 200,000 migrating snow geese; a driving loop and trails cover the rest of the year.

name: Indian Echo Caverns
blurb: Limestone show cave in a bluff above Swatara Creek near Hershey, open daily for guided tours.

facts.fee: paid guided tour

name: Wildwood Park
blurb: Marshy lake on the north edge of Harrisburg circled by a flat loop of paved path and boardwalk, with a nature center. Good for herons, egrets and lotus blooms.

name: Fort Hunter Mansion and Park
blurb: Riverside county park around a stone mansion, with big old trees and a view upstream to the Rockville Bridge, the longest stone-arch railroad viaduct ever built.

name: Negley Park
blurb: Neighborhood park on a bluff across the Susquehanna from Harrisburg, with a head-on view of the skyline, the Capitol dome and the river bridges.

name: Boyd Big Tree Preserve Conservation Area
blurb: 1,025 acres of mature forest on the slope of Blue Mountain north of Harrisburg, set aside for its large trees, with a network of loop trails.

name: Peters Mountain: Table Rock (Appalachian Trail)
blurb: Ridge walk on the Appalachian Trail from the PA 225 crossing to a rock ledge overlooking Clarks Valley.

name: Hawk Rock (Duncannon)
blurb: Steep Appalachian Trail climb up stone steps on Cove Mountain to a ledge over Duncannon and the meeting of the Juniata and Susquehanna rivers.

name: Waggoner's Gap Hawk Watch
blurb: Rock pile on the spine of Kittatinny Ridge, a short walk from the PA 74 summit lot, where counters tally migrating hawks and eagles from August through December.

name: Flat Rock (Colonel Denning State Park)
blurb: Rocky climb of more than 900 ft from the park to an outcrop on Blue Mountain with a 180-degree view of the Cumberland Valley. Cool off afterward at the park's small lake beach.

name: Opossum Lake
blurb: Quiet fishing lake below Blue Mountain west of Carlisle with a shoreline trail and electric-motor-only boating.

name: Hemlocks Natural Area
blurb: 120 acres of old-growth hemlock in a narrow ravine of Tuscarora State Forest, a National Natural Landmark. Trails follow Patterson Run under the big trees.

name: Big Spring State Forest Picnic Area
blurb: Picnic stop on PA 274 with a trail to a railroad tunnel that was started into Conococheague Mountain and never finished.

name: Little Buffalo State Park
blurb: 923-acre park around Holman Lake with a covered bridge, a restored working grist mill, a swimming pool and lakeside trails.

name: Box Huckleberry Natural Area
blurb: Ten-acre woodlot protecting a single colony of box huckleberry more than 1,000 years old, on a short interpretive loop. The smallest state forest natural area in Pennsylvania.

name: Cowans Gap State Park
blurb: Mountain lake with a sand beach in a gap of Tuscarora Mountain, surrounded by Buchanan State Forest. Steep trails climb from the shore to ridge overlooks.

name: Big Mountain Overlook
blurb: Open ledge and stone shelter on the Tuscarora Trail at the high point of Tuscarora Mountain, reached by a gravel forest road and a short walk south of Cowans Gap.

name: Buchanan's Birthplace State Park
blurb: Pyramid of native stone in a wooded hollow below Tuscarora Mountain, marking the cabin site where President James Buchanan was born. An 18.5-acre park with a trout stream and picnic tables.

name: Martin's Mill Covered Bridge
blurb: 205-ft Town lattice truss covered bridge built in 1849 over Conococheague Creek, in a small township park open dawn to dusk.

name: Jarrett Falls and Meadow Grounds Lake
blurb: Trail from the dam of a 204-acre mountain lake on State Game Lands 53 down Roaring Run to a set of waterfalls.

name: Abandoned Pennsylvania Turnpike: Rays Hill Tunnel
blurb: Cracked four-lane highway left to the weeds since 1968, now walked and biked as the Old PA Pike Trail. From the Breezewood end it is a short ride to the unlit 3,532-ft Rays Hill Tunnel. Bring lights.

name: Abandoned Pennsylvania Turnpike: Sideling Hill Tunnel
blurb: The longer abandoned tunnel, 6,782 ft and pitch dark in the middle, toward the eastern end of the old turnpike. No services, rough pavement, cold air pouring from the portals.

name: Trough Creek State Park
blurb: Narrow gorge with a run of oddities along one road: Balanced Rock perched on a cliff edge, Rainbow Falls, a suspension bridge and the Ice Mine, a pit that holds ice into summer.

name: Thousand Steps
blurb: More than 1,000 stone steps laid by quarry workers in the 1930s, straight up Jacks Mountain from a US 22 pull-off to quarry ledges and views over the Juniata River.

name: Big Savage Tunnel (Great Allegheny Passage)
blurb: The longest tunnel on the Great Allegheny Passage, lit inside, with a wide valley view just outside its southern portal. Closed roughly December 15 to April 10 each winter.

name: Blue Blazes Whiskey Still (Catoctin Mountain Park)
blurb: Short creekside trail from the visitor center to a moonshine still exhibit at the site of a large Prohibition-era operation raided in 1929.

name: Bickle Knob Observation Tower
blurb: One of the last climbable observation towers in Monongahela National Forest, on a summit east of Elkins near the south end of Otter Creek Wilderness. Road access in the warm months.

name: Roaring Plains West Wilderness
blurb: The high, wet plateau just south of Dolly Sods: 6,820 acres of spruce, bog and rim-edge rock with long canyon views and far fewer people. Trails are faint and partly unmarked; carry a map and GPS track.
coord_source: wikipedia (centre of the wilderness, not a trailhead)

name: Union Canal Tunnel Park
blurb: Hand-dug canal tunnel from the 1820s, counted as the oldest transportation tunnel still standing in the country, with a towpath walk beside a watered stretch of the old Union Canal.

name: Swatara State Park
blurb: 3,520-acre park along 8 miles of Swatara Creek with a long rail trail, old canal remains and a roadside shale pit where visitors may dig for fossils.
